subject: BrightLane — Order Form & SLA redlines
messages:
From: Jack Walters <jack.walters@brightlane.com>

Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 13:12:00 -04:00
Subject: BrightLane — Order Form & SLA redlines

Kim,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Legal at BrightLane asked us to capture a couple of items in the Order Form and MSA before we sign. I attached the latest Order Form (v3) with inline redlines — most of the notes are around the SLA section. High level:

- BrightLane is asking for a 99.95% monthly uptime target for the paid tier (we are currently seeing 99.9 in the draft).
- They want a cap on monthly service credits to be 10% of monthly fees but also want a minimum credit of 2% if the uptime falls below the threshold.
- Response times for Sev1 incidents: they propose 15 minutes instead of Redwood's 30 minutes.
- They requested a defined maintenance blackout for end-of-quarter deploys (they want no scheduled maintenance in the last 3 business days of quarter close).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can accept these items or propose alternatives? I'm copying procurement for billing visibility.

Attachments: BrightLane_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf, 1 page summary + redlines)

Appreciate a quick read — we are trying to close before September 20.

Thanks,
Jack
Jack Walters
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
BrightLane Analytics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jack Walters <jack.walters@brightlane.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane — Order Form & SLA redlines

Jack — thanks for sending and for the clear summary. Putting internal owners on thread to accelerate: Aditya (Legal) and Marissa (Ops). Rishi, looping you for billing/credit impact modeling.

I reviewed the redlines quickly and attached a short Redwood markup (SLA_KP_v1.docx) with our starting positions. Quick thoughts:

- Uptime target: 99.95% is a reasonable ask on paper but implies different capacity/reservation requirements. We can propose 99.95% for a dedicated/reserved tier (Dedicated), and 99.9% for hosted pay-as-you-go — that gives BrightLane a path without immediate capacity reservation.
- Service credits: We can accept a floor credit (e.g., minimum 2% for an outage tier) but we need a monthly cap tied to the contract tier. Propose a sliding cap: 5% for hosted, 10% for Dedicated with a max-of-three-month aggregated cap.
- Response times: 15-minute response for Sev1 is aggressive for hosted unless we include priority headroom and an on-call SLA. Legal — is there a way to phrase response vs. resolution? We should keep response (acknowledge) at 15m for Dedicated customers but resolution times remain dependent on incident severity and root cause.
- Maintenance windows: we cannot guarantee no scheduled maintenance during quarter-close windows across all regions, but we can agree to no scheduled maintenance for customer-impacting changes during BrightLane’s defined blackout period if they commit to a maintenance notice period (e.g., 14 days) and allow for emergency maintenance with advance notice when possible.

Next steps I propose:
1) Aditya to provide redline language for Order Form & SLA (targeting the capacity carveouts above).
2) Ops (Marissa + Rishi) to confirm cost/delta for 99.95% Dedicated tier and provide a sample credit calculation for BrightLane's monthly spend.
3) Joint redline session early next week with BrightLane legal if they are available (we can use a shared doc).

Attach: SLA_KP_v1.docx (Redwood initial positions)

If that works, I can schedule a 45m call Thursday or Friday.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane — Order Form & SLA redlines

Kimberly / Jack — I reviewed Jack's redlines and Kimberly's proposed carveouts. I attached a comment table with proposed contract language and the legal rationale. Key items:

- Uptime definition: we should be explicit that uptime is measured per calendar month, on a per-region basis, excluding force majeure and customer-caused outages. We will accept 99.95% for a Dedicated reservation that is explicitly defined in the Order Form (commit tiers, sustained throughput).
- Service credit calculation: recommend formula of (Monthly Fee * outage_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) capped at the tier cap. This is easier to audit and limits disputes. Avoid flat percentage floors that are not tied to actual downtime minutes.
- Credit cap: I can agree to a floor credit approach only if BrightLane accepts a higher cap for Dedicated (10%) and a three-month aggregation clause. Also want to add an annual cap on credits to guard tail risk (e.g., cumulative credits cannot exceed 30% of 12 months' fees).
- Response vs. resolution: we can accept a 15-minute response acknowledgement for Dedicated customers if they accept the Incident Classification table (attached). Resolution SLAs are contingent and we prefer to remove hard resolution guarantees.
- Maintenance blackout: we can agree to BrightLane's blackout if they provide an annual calendar of blackout dates at least 60 days out and allow a 30-day exception for critical security patches.

Attaching: Redwood_SLA_comment_table.xlsx (line-item language suggestions).

I suggest a joint legal/ops call Fri 11 Sep 2026 or Mon 14 Sep 2026 to walk table rows and align on language. Jack — can you confirm availability?

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Jack Walters <jack.walters@brightlane.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane — Order Form & SLA redlines

Kim / Aditya — thanks for the quick review and the detailed positions. BrightLane can flex on a couple of points to get this across the finish line:

- We will accept the Dedicated carveout for 99.95% uptime (we had capacity certainty concerns). Please indicate in Order Form how Dedicated is procured and the expected lead time.
- For credits: BrightLane will accept a minutes-based formula (good compromise) but asks that the monthly minimum credit be no less than 2% of monthly fees if uptime falls below 99.5% in a month. We can live with a reasonable cap (10%) for Dedicated.
- Response times: we can accept 15-minute acknowledge for Dedicated; we understand Redwood's pushback on hard resolution SLAs.
- Maintenance blackout: BrightLane will provide a quarterly blackout calendar and can accept a 30-day exception window for critical security updates.

We are available Monday 14 Sep after 16:00 ET for a joint session (we can do a quick 30–45m). If those concessions are acceptable, procurement can issue a clean redline and DocuSign afterwards.

Thanks — Jack
